changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/console-form-container-specs-one-declaration-5596.md`

- names `FormPage.tsx` → `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` — edited by this change

  > objectui#5542 converged the LEAF of this contract — the field spec — and left the two containers above it untouched, because converging them was a bigger call than a mechanical import. `FormSectionSpec` and `FormViewSpec` were each hand-declared twice under the same names, once in `packages/app-shell`'s `SchemaForm.tsx` and once in `apps/console`'s `FormPage.tsx`. Unlike the leaf — whose console copy was a clean subset — these two had **already drifted, in both directions**, so neither copy was a subset of the other and there were two live answers to "what may an author write":

### `.changeset/console-form-field-spec-one-declaration-5542.md`

- names `FormPage.tsx` → `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` — edited by this change

  > objectui#5040 was not a missing key. It was that **two hand-written descriptions of one contract drifted**, and nothing could notice, because each was only ever checked against itself. PR #5537 converged the two app-shell descriptions into `views/metadata-admin/form-spec.ts`. A **third** survived in `apps/console`: `FormPage.tsx` declared its own nine-key `interface FormFieldSpec`, under the same name, in a different package — so the same failure mode stayed fully available.

### `.changeset/console-formpage-runtime-default-seed-5727.md`

- names `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` → `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `readPrefill` in `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` seeded every declared default unconditionally. A `defaultValue` may be a literal, or an *instruction* the server resolves per insert — a `DEFAULT_VALUE_TOKENS` token (`NOW()`, `current_user`) or a CEL Expression envelope. Seeding one of those literally put the text `NOW()` into a datetime input on both `/forms/:name` and the public `/f/:slug` route, and submitting it sent that string as the field's value — which is neither absent nor null, so `ObjectQL.applyFieldDefaults` never resolved the declared default and the column stored the token text instead of a timestamp.

### `.changeset/console-formpage-visible-predicates-5594.md`

- names `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` → `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` is a **second, independent form renderer** — its own `buildSections`, its own JSX — and it serves both the public `/f/:slug` route and the internal `/forms/:name` route. It read neither spelling of the FormView field visibility predicate: a repo-wide grep for a `visibleWhen` / `visibleOn` *read* inside that file returned zero. So a field an author conditioned on `record.priority == 'urgent'` — legal, spec-strict metadata that `@objectstack/spec` normalises to `visibleWhen` (ADR-0089), and that the metadata-admin designer both authors and honours — rendered unconditionally on both routes. Fail-open and silent: the author saw the field always, with no diagnostic.

- names `FormPage.tsx` → `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` — edited by this change

  > objectui#2212 recorded this exact symptom and PR #2214 fixed it — in a **different chain**: `ModalForm` → `resolveFormViewLayout` → `@object-ui/plugin-form` `sectionFields.ts` → `@object-ui/components` `renderers/form/form.tsx`. `FormPage.tsx` is on that chain at no point, and #2212's regression pin lives with the chain it fixed, so nothing in the suite could see this copy. One contract, two implementations, each only ever checked against itself.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `3ed3eec08` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1333 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1906 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36051993692)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `532aaa8ba850cc211a1cca3ca1e6d426f12a3e89`

Rendered by an isolated review subagent spawned by the `domain:ui#4` seat; its served tier was checked against its transcript stamps (88 of 88 at the review tier). Adopted by this seat.

### ① Derived judgments

- **(a) Marker hidden from the tree only, still visible.** At head the row label renders `state.required && span.ml-0.5.text-destructive[aria-hidden="true"]` with text `*`; no `hidden`, `sr-only` or display class was added, so the glyph still paints. Confirmed indirectly by two pre-existing pins that read the label's `textContent` for `*` (`FormPage.conditionalRules.test.tsx`, `FormPage.predicateScope.test.tsx`): `aria-hidden` leaves `textContent` intact, so they stay valid and green.
- **(a) Required channel per arm at head** (the `common` object carries `required: state.required` and is spread into every hand-rolled non-checkbox, non-radio, non-file control):
  - `textarea` / `paragraph` / `long_text` — `textarea`, native `required` via `common`.
  - `number` / `integer` / `decimal` / `currency` — `input type=number`, native `required`.
  - `email`, `url`, `password`, `date`, `time` — `input`, native `required`.
  - `datetime` / `timestamp` — `input type=datetime-local`, native `required`.
  - `select` / `picklist` / `enum` — `select`, native `required` (plus the placeholder option `disabled={state.required}`).
  - `default` (text and any unknown type) — `input type=text`, native `required`.
  - `file` — shared `FileWidget`, `aria-required={state.required || undefined}` (pre-existing, unchanged).
  - `boolean` / `toggle` / `checkbox` — `input type=checkbox`, NEW `aria-required={state.required || undefined}`; base carried neither channel (base arm: `id, name, type, disabled, checked, onChange, className` only). React renders `aria-required="true"` for `true` and omits the attribute for `undefined`, which the two CONTROL cases pin.
  - `radio` — inputs carry no `id`, no `required`, no `aria-required`; the row label's `htmlFor=f_NAME` names no element. The diff has exactly two hunks in `FormPage.tsx` (checkbox `aria-required`, label marker) and neither touches this arm, so the radio gap is pre-existing and unchanged. Out of scope is the right call: `aria-required` is not supported on role `radio`; the repair needs a `radiogroup` container.
- **(a) Shape matches the cited rule.** `packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionParamDialog.tsx` marks its `*` `aria-hidden="true"` with the exact "Visual-only (objectui#3299)" wording, and its boolean branch puts `aria-required={param.required || undefined}` on the checkbox control, so the PR's checkbox choice is the same shape, not a new one.
- **(b) `aria-required` vs native `required` on the checkbox.** `isMissingForRequired` (`packages/core/src/validation/required-presence.ts`) returns true only for `undefined`, `null`, blank string, or empty array; its docblock names `false` as a real value and cites cloud#972 for the "must be TRUE" failure mode. `FormPage`'s `<form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>` has no `noValidate`, and `handleSubmit` performs no client-side required check (it only runs `omitServerOwnedBlanks`, which composes `isRuntimeDefault && isMissingForRequired` through `@object-ui/plugin-form`'s `omitServerResolvedDefaults`, then submits). So browser constraint validation is live: native `required` on the checkbox would make the browser refuse an unchecked required boolean that the presence rule and the server accept. `aria-required` is not part of constraint validation and changes nothing in the submit path. Judgment confirmed. Minor looseness, PR body only (not the changeset): "the required rule this page reads" is reached through the server-owned-blank filter rather than a direct required check; the semantics claimed are still correct.
- **(c) Nothing else depends on the old `LABEL *` name.** `git grep` at head over `apps/console` and root `e2e/` for `name: '... *'`, `name: /...\*/`, `getByLabelText('... *')`, `toHaveAccessibleName('...*')`, `Title *` returns nothing outside the new pin. `apps/console/e2e` does not exist. The only `*` assertions on FormPage labels read `textContent` (see above), which is unaffected.
- **(d) The pin is real and can fail.** `apps/console/src/__tests__/formPageRequiredMarker-10178.test.tsx` renders the real `FormPage` (`mode="internal"`, imported by relative path, no dist) inside `MemoryRouter` on `/forms/:name` with stubbed `fetch` for `/meta/view/` and `/meta/object/`. Positive cases assert the computed accessible name via jest-dom `toHaveAccessibleName('Title')` and `getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Title' })`, `toBeRequired()`, and for the checkbox `toHaveAccessibleName(expect.not.stringContaining('*'))`, `aria-required="true"`, and no native `required`. Two CONTROL cases (optional text, optional checkbox) assert no marker and no required state, so neither "drop the marker" nor "mark everything required" passes. The `aria-hidden="true"` attribute assertion does restate the fix, but it sits beside the behavioural name assertion, which cannot be satisfied by restating. The reported 2 RED / 2 GREEN on base is consistent with the base markup (`Title *` from the bare span; checkbox with no `aria-required`), and the 1 RED ablation matches deleting only the checkbox attribute. Pin placement follows the claim's `apps/console/src/**/__tests__` (33 sibling tests there) rather than the beside-component convention of the other FormPage pins; harmless, collected by the console project's default include.
- **(e) Changeset sentences vs code.** `/f/:slug` and `/forms/:name` route to `FormPage` (`apps/console/src/App.tsx`) — true. Marker was a `*` inside the `label` — true at base. "Title *" announced — matches the happy-dom name; Chromium gives `Title*`, same defect. `aria-hidden` now, the rule `ActionParamDialog` follows (objectui#3299) — true. Text-like, number, date/time, select, textarea already native `required` — true via `common`. `file` already `aria-required` — true. Checkbox carried neither, now `aria-required` — true. Not native `required` because on a checkbox it means must-be-checked and the rule counts `false` as a value — true of `isMissingForRequired`. No line-address citations. Cosmetic only: one paragraph has an unwrapped long line.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@object-ui/console` is correct in both shape and level. `apps/console/package.json` has no `private` field, `publishConfig.access: public`, version `17.6.0`, and `@object-ui/console` is listed in `.changeset/config.json` `fixed` (not in `ignore`); `apps/console/CHANGELOG.md` is populated. AGENTS.md line 167 requires a changeset for any `src/` edit in a `fixed`-group package "including `apps/console`", reserving empty frontmatter for internal or test-only edits; this PR changes published renderer source with a user-visible a11y fix, so a named bump is required, not empty frontmatter. Convention evidence on `origin/main`: `10167-formpage-file-field-arm.md` (console-only FormPage fix) is `'@object-ui/console': patch`, and `10193-language-reset-on-owner-change.md` lists `'@object-ui/console': patch`. AGENTS.md lines 259–261: patch/minor evolve independently, `major` is banned (CI `check-changeset-no-major`, reported and shown green as "Changeset Bump Policy"). A bug fix with no API or export change is `patch`, not `minor`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `Fixes #10178` is appropriate: the card asks for the marker to be `aria-hidden` (or the accessible name to be clean) on `FormPage`, with a probe; both halves are delivered and pinned. The card's "worth sweeping" other renderers is explicitly marked outside the radius; the dev filed them as out-of-scope findings in the report.
- Closing keywords: the only one in the PR body is `Fixes #10178`. `objectui#10179` appears only as "remains open. It is not addressed here"; `objectui#3299` appears as a rule citation; `objectui#3962` is not in the PR text at all. Commit message references `objectui#3299` without a keyword. None of #10179, #3299, #3962 is closed by keyword.
- Model identifiers: none in commit title/body, trailers, PR title or PR body (scanned for the model and version token family). Trailers are `Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` and `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01BP8CMtACxTdLjqR6rhd33C`; footer is the session-URL form. Brand name only, no model name, which matches the os-dev.md "model-free trailer pair" rule.
- File surface matches the claim exactly: `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` (12+/1−, two hunks: label marker `aria-hidden` and checkbox `aria-required`, both named in the claim), one pin `apps/console/src/__tests__/formPageRequiredMarker-10178.test.tsx`, one changeset `.changeset/10178-formpage-required-marker-aria-hidden.md`. Three files, nothing else. Single commit, parent is the merge-base `1f8ef0a89` (the reported BASE).
